hook: After the United States annexed Texas, a quarrel over its border and President Polk's wish for California and New Mexico brought war with Mexico.

sides.who: The United States regular army, state volunteers and navy, with American settlers of the Bear Flag revolt in California
The Mexican Republic's army and national guard, though only 7 of its 19 states sent men, arms or money

resultLine: Scott's army took Mexico City in September 1847, and the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo, signed on 2 February 1848, handed Mexico's northern lands to the United States.

strategies.name: Flying artillery
strategies.text: At Palo Alto in May 1846, American gunners fired their light cannon, galloped to a new spot and fired again. They outgunned the Mexican artillery and broke up cavalry charges.

strategies.name: Scott's landing at Veracruz
strategies.text: Striking at the heart of Mexico, Scott landed his army on the beach near Veracruz in March 1847 without losing a man, took the port after twenty days and marched inland on the capital.

strategies.name: A nation divided
strategies.text: Mexico changed presidents four times in 1846, liberals and conservatives fought each other, and conservatives revolted in early 1847 against seizing Church property to pay for the war.

impact: Mexico lost about 55 percent of its territory, some 525,000 square miles, for $15 million.
The United States now reached the Pacific, taking in California, Nevada, Utah and parts of several future states.
The fight over slavery in the new lands, begun with the Wilmot Proviso, deepened the split that led to civil war.

sources.title: Office of the Historian: The Annexation of Texas, the Mexican-American War, and the Treaty of Guadalupe-Hidalgo, 1845–1848
